Without the answer options, I can't pick one, but the strongest candidate is that the calculus assumes all pleasures and pains lie on a single commensurable scale that can be summed, and experience gives little reason to think they do. The shared note's claim, that pleasure and pain are inevitable features of life, doesn't refute the calculus because the calculus takes them as its inputs. Paste the options and I'll choose the strongest one.
